name: holoocean-directional-wind
exact_failure: The packaged HoloOcean 2.3.0 SurfaceVessel interface has no public external-force command. Its control input is two fixed longitudinal thruster forces, which span surge and yaw but cannot produce an independent lateral aerodynamic force.

wind_path.requested: arbitrary horizontal wind direction from a 0-5 m/s magnitude draw
wind_path.existing_mapping: longitudinal force is divided equally between the two native fixed thrusters

why_current_is_not_a_template: Ocean current is a native environment vector accepted by set_ocean_currents. Wind is a force on the vessel and the packaged API exposes neither an arbitrary body-force input nor a lateral actuator channel.

lower_level_api_investigation.standard_command_api: No AddForce/ApplyForce rigid-body command is exposed by the documented command set.
lower_level_api_investigation.custom_world_command: CustomCommand can only invoke a command name implemented by the loaded Unreal world; it does not itself provide a force primitive.
lower_level_api_investigation.custom_dynamics: SurfaceVessel control scheme 2 accepts a six-axis global acceleration vector, but disables native gravity, buoyancy, damping, and all other forces except collisions.
lower_level_api_investigation.assessment: Custom Dynamics would replace the validated native SurfaceVessel plant rather than add wind to it. Using it requires rebuilding the complete vehicle dynamics and is outside a directional-wind wiring fix.

prohibited_workaround: Do not convert lateral wind into differential thrust or yaw; that changes the requested force direction and is not literal contract enforcement.
scoping_decision_required: Either extend and rebuild the HoloOcean Unreal package with an additive rigid-body force command, or document directional wind as a genuine HoloOcean capability gap.
